newsitem.title: CHINA: BANKS WITHDRAW FACILITIES FROM IWAI'S.
newsitem.headline: BANKS WITHDRAW FACILITIES FROM IWAI'S.

text.p: Iwai International Holdings Ltd said two of its three principal bankers had withdrawn banking facilities worth HK$21 million from its subsidiaries, but Iwai was able to meet outstanding financial obligations.

The company said in a statement on Tuesday that it was not yet in a position to ascertain the impact of the withdrawal on its long term cash flow position in the absence of further facilities provided through its shareholder Heng Fung Holdings Co Ltd or other banks, but said the group was solvent.

Iwai's International's outstanding loans totalled HK$8.7 million on July 20 but HK$3 million had been repaid on July 29 through short term loans extended by Heng Fung Finance, a subsidiary of Heng Fung Holdings.

The company said Heng Fung was helping in negotiations with its bankers to secure loans for the Iwai Group and would continue to provide funds for the group's short term working capital and repayment of the outstanding loans by August 30.
The provision of funds for the Iwai Group would not have any adverse effect on Heng Fung's financial position, it said.
Trading in Iwai's International shares was suspended on Monday and due to resume on Tuesday.
The stock last traded at HK$1.67.
